CommonTrapReference: T4: Applying joint costs to sell-or-process-further
ExplanationCorrect: The IMA framework treats EVPI as a ceiling on information spending: it is the most Harbor should pay for perfect foresight before deciding. Paying less than EVPI can be worthwhile; paying more destroys value even with flawless information. Joint or shared history costs are irrelevant to this forward-looking ceiling.
ExplanationWrongB: The expected profit of the project is the baseline EV without information, only one input to the comparison. EVPI is the improvement that perfect foresight adds over that baseline.
ExplanationWrongC: The probability of the good outcome weights the branches but is not itself the information value. EVPI combines probabilities, payoffs, and the without-information alternative.
ExplanationWrongD: The sunk cost of gathering data is already spent and excluded. EVPI guides future spending on information; it never includes historical outlays.

CommonTrapReference: T2: Using absorption costing unit cost for special-order pricing
ExplanationCorrect: Expected value decomposes each branch into probability-weighted payoffs net of incremental outlay. Launch EV = 0.50 x $150,000 + 0.50 x $18,000 = $75,000 + $9,000 = $84,000. Waiting yields $61,000 and licensing $55,000. Launching maximizes EV at $84,000; the full-cost absorption figure is irrelevant since only incremental launch spending differs. A common trap is loading sunk development overhead into the launch branch.
ExplanationWrongA: Launch at EV $73,000 deducts an $11,000 sunk development allocation from the branch. Sunk overhead applies to all alternatives equally and must be excluded.
ExplanationWrongB: Waiting at $61,000 is correctly valued but is not the maximum. The $84,000 launch EV dominates waiting by $23,000.
ExplanationWrongC: Licensing at $55,000 is correctly valued but trails launching. The decision rule selects the maximum EV, which is the $84,000 launch branch.

ExplanationCorrect: EVPI is the difference between deciding with and without foresight across three demand states. EV without = $118,000 (best blind alternative) and EV with perfect information = $165,000, so EVPI = $165,000 - $118,000 = $47,000. ExplanationWrongC: Skipping on EVPI of $18,000 miscomputes EVwPI by omitting the moderate branch entirely. All three demand states must be weighted in the with-information total.
